sourceRecovery.title: Recover an original file
sourceRecovery.intro: These are byte-for-byte copies made before overwriting files. Export a copy to a location you choose. Recovery keeps the current document and backup intact.
sourceRecovery.empty: No originals have been backed up on this device.

folderPrompt.title: Choose a Backup Folder
folderPrompt.introBackup: Backups are dated copies of your script, kept in a folder outside OpenDraft — so they survive whatever happens to the app. Choose where they go and this script is backed up straight away. You can change the folder later in Settings ▸ Backups.
folderPrompt.introOpen: Backups are dated copies of your script, kept in a folder outside OpenDraft — so they survive whatever happens to the app. Choose where they go. You can change the folder later in Settings ▸ Backups.
folderPrompt.autoHint: To have OpenDraft also back up on its own while you write, turn on automatic backups in Settings ▸ Backups.

recoveryPrompt.title: Recover unsaved changes?
recoveryPrompt.found: OpenDraft found unsaved changes to {{title}} from your last session, edited {{when}}.
recoveryPrompt.sameDocument: Restoring replaces what is currently in the editor. Your last saved version stays untouched until you save again.
recoveryPrompt.otherDocument: These changes belong to a different screenplay than the one open now. Restoring opens them as an unsaved document, so nothing you have saved is overwritten — use Save As to keep them.

backupSettings.chooseWritable: Choose a folder OpenDraft can write to first
backupSettings.title: Automatic Backups
backupSettings.webOnly: Timed backups write files to a folder you choose, which needs the OpenDraft app — a browser tab cannot hold on to a folder. In the browser, use File → Export → OpenDraft (.odraft) to save a copy wherever you like.
backupSettings.description: OpenDraft can save timestamped copies of your script to a folder you choose while you write. Each project gets its own folder inside it, and the first copy is written as soon as you turn this on. Backups live outside the app's database, so they survive even if something happens to it. This is separate from Version History, which stores checkpoints inside the database.
backupSettings.mobileHint: Pick somewhere outside the app — a folder in Files, iCloud Drive, Google Drive or Dropbox — so your backups survive if OpenDraft is ever removed or reinstalled.
backupSettings.oneDrive: This folder is inside OneDrive. Cloud sync can interfere with files as they're written — a local folder is safer for backups.
backupSettings.leaveHint: A copy is also written whenever you leave OpenDraft, so work is saved before the system suspends the app.
backupSettings.keepHint: Applies per script. Backups you make yourself with Back Up Now are never deleted automatically.
backupSettings.includeImagesHint: Makes backups larger, but a restored script comes back complete. Without this, images in a restored script will be missing.
backupSettings.unsaved: Also back up documents I haven't saved yet
